propositions.text: The appellants are Colombian citizens appealing an RPD decision denying refugee protection.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX (Principal Appellant) and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX (Associate Appellants) are citizens of Colombia. They are appealing a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) denying their claim for refugee protection

propositions.text: The appellants seek a finding as Convention refugees under s. 96 or persons in need of protection under s. 97 of the Act.
propositions.quote: and are asking the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to find them to be Convention refugees under s. 96 or persons in need of protection under s. 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Act).

propositions.text: The RPD decision was signed January 15, 2020 and received January 21, 2020.
propositions.quote: The notice of decision was signed on January 15, 2020 and was received by the Appellants on January 21, 2020.

propositions.text: Appellant alleges targeting by Black Eagles due to social activism and political involvement; father threatened and assaulted.
propositions.quote: According to their Basis of Claim (BOC), Appellant XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX (XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX) has been targeted by the "Aguilas Negras" (Black Eagles) because of his social activism with a XXXX XXXX organization as well as his political involvement in helping a candidate in an election. He also alleges that his father was threatened and assaulted because of his activities.

propositions.text: Appellants fear for their lives if returned to Colombia.
propositions.quote: The Appellants fear for their lives should they return to Colombia.

propositions.text: RPD rejected claim for lack of credibility and found Black Eagles lacked means and motivation to target appellant.
propositions.quote: The RPD rejected their claim of refugee protection for lack of credibility. It concluded that the Black Eagles did not have the means nor the motivation to target XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Appellants submitted additional evidence about Black Eagles and argued RPD erred in credibility assessment and omitted analysis under ss. 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: In their Memorandum of Appeal, the Appellants submitted additional evidence about the Black Eagles. They argued that the RPD erred in its assessment of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX's credibility and omitted to conduct an analysis of under sections 96 and 97 of the Act.

propositions.text: The determinative issue for the RAD is credibility.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue for the RAD is credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellants are Colombians appealing the RPD's denial of refugee protection, alleging targeting by Black Eagles and fearing return; RPD rejected claim for lack of credibility; appellants argue RPD erred; credibility is the key issue.

propositions.text: Pursuant to s. 111(1)(a) of the Act, RAD confirms RPD decision denying refugee protection; appeals dismissed.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to Section 111(1)(a) of the Act, the RAD confirms the decision of the RPD that the Appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection. The appeals are dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms the RPD decision denying protection and dismisses the appeals under s. 111(1)(a) of the Act.

propositions.text: Appellants submitted newspaper articles postdating RPD decision, arguing they meet s. 110(4) requirements as material and relevant evidence about Black Eagles.
propositions.quote: The Appellants submitted several newspaper articles with their Memorandum of Appeal. They argue that the evidence postdates the RPD's decision and as such, meets the requirements of subsection 110(4) of the Act. According to their submission, the evidence is material and relevant as it relates to the existence of the Black Eagles and their presence throughout Colombia.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants submit newspaper articles postdating the RPD decision, arguing they are material and relevant evidence under s. 110(4).

propositions.text: Only evidence that arose after RPD decision, was not reasonably available then, or could not reasonably have been expected to be brought before RPD is admissible.
propositions.quote: According to the law,2 I can only accept evidence that: i. arose after the RPD decision; or ii. was not reasonably available at the time of the decision; or iii. that you could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to bring to the RPD before the decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the legal rule limiting admissible evidence on appeal to new or previously unavailable evidence.

propositions.text: New evidence postdating RPD decision will be assessed on its content, not just its date.
propositions.quote: In the case of new evidence that post-dates the RPD's decision, I will assess the evidence based on the information it contains, and not only the date of the document.

paragraphs.summary: The court will assess new evidence based on its content, not merely its date.

propositions.text: Evidence meeting admissibility criteria must be new, credible and relevant to be accepted.
propositions.quote: If the evidence meets one or more of the requirements set out in paragraph 4, I must decide if the evidence is new, credible and relevant before I can accept it.

paragraphs.summary: The court must decide if evidence is new, credible and relevant before accepting it.

propositions.text: The news articles submitted are not admissible as new evidence for various reasons including irrelevance and availability before RPD decision.
propositions.quote: I find the news articles submitted by the Appellants are not admissible as new evidence. My reasons follow.

propositions.text: Article Feb 7, 2020 about Black Eagles threats to journalists and politicians is irrelevant to appellant who is neither.
propositions.quote: Colombia: Paramilitary Black Eagles Threaten Social Activists, February 7, 2020: This article post-dates the RPD's decision. However, the article mentions threats against journalists and politicians in favor of national strikes. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is neither a journalist nor a politician and does not allege having any involvement with the organization or participation in national strikes. The article is therefore not relevant as it is incapable of proving any of the allegations made by the Appellants.

propositions.text: Article Feb 14 with no year is not shown to be unavailable before RPD decision and thus inadmissible.
propositions.quote: End of Political Violence and Threats Advocated in Colombia, February 14; This article has no year of publication and it is not possible to determine if it post-dates the RPD's decision. While I note that it refers to an event taking place on October 11, 2019, the Appellants have not demonstrated that they were unable to obtain this article before the RPD's decision nor that they would not have reasonably been expected to provide the article before the RPD's decision. It is therefore not admissible on appeal in accordance with ss. 110(4) of the Act.

propositions.text: Article Feb 13, 2020 on xenophobia postdates RPD decision but info was available before, so inadmissible.
propositions.quote: Venezuelan Migrants Face Rising Xenophobia in Latin America, February 13, 2020; This article post-dates the RPD's decision. However, the information it contains did not arise after the RPD rejection and was reasonably available for the Appellants to present to the RPD. It is therefore not admissible in evidence as it does not meet the statutory requirements of ss. 110(4) of the Act.

propositions.text: HRW report article Jan 22, 2020 postdates RPD decision but info was available before, so inadmissible.
propositions.quote: HRW: Armed Groups Move Freely on Colombia-Venezuela Border, January 22, 2020; This article about a Human Rights Watch Report post-dates the RPD's decision but it contains information about activities which took place before the decision. The evidence was reasonably available to present to the RPD. It is therefore not admissible as evidence because it does not meet the statutory requirements under ss. 110(4) of the Act.

propositions.text: Article Jan 21, 2020 postdates RPD decision but info was available before, so inadmissible.
propositions.quote: Everybody in Colombia Can Guess Who the Aguilas Negras Are, Except the Aguilas Negras, January 21, 2020; The article post-dates the RPD's decision. However, it does not meet the requirements of ss. 110(4) of the Act because the information it contains did not arise after the RPD rejection of the claim and was reasonably available for the Appellants to present to the RPD. It is therefore not admissible on appeal.

propositions.text: Article Feb 6, 2020 about Black Eagles threats to FARC leaders is irrelevant to appellant who is neither leader nor militant, so inadmissible.
propositions.quote: Black Eagles, The Name with Which Criminals Are Camouflaged? February 6, 2020; This article post-dates the RPD's decision and contains information about threats made against the national leaders and militants of the FARC Party. However, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is neither a national leader nor a militant of the FARC Party and therefore the article is not relevant to his claim. The evidence is not admissible on Appeal as it does not me

paragraphs.summary: The court finds all submitted news articles inadmissible as new evidence due to irrelevance or availability before the RPD decision.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD decision based on negative credibility and that news articles justify a hearing under s. 110(6).
propositions.quote: The Appellants submit that the RPD based its decision on negative credibility findings and that, based on the news articles about the existence of the Black Eagles included with their Memorandum, the RAD should hold a hearing under ss. 110(6) of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the negative credibility findings and news articles justify a hearing under s. 110(6).

propositions.text: Ss. 110(3) requires RAD to proceed without hearing on RPD record but allows documentary evidence and submissions from parties.
propositions.quote: Ss. 110(3) of the Act requires that the RAD proceed without a hearing, on the basis of the RPD's record, while allowing the RAD to accept documentary evidence and submissions from the Minister and the Appellants.

propositions.text: Ss. 110(4) limits evidence to that arising after rejection or not reasonably available or expected before rejection.
propositions.quote: The person, who is the subject of the appeal may, pursuant to ss. 110(4) of the Act, present only evidence that arose after the rejection of their claim or that was not reasonably available, or that the person could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented, at the time of the rejection.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains ss. 110(3) requires proceeding without hearing but allows documentary evidence; ss. 110(4) limits evidence to new or unavailable evidence.

propositions.text: Ss. 110(6) allows RAD to hold hearing if new documentary evidence raises serious credibility issue central to RPD decision and could justify claim outcome.
propositions.quote: According to ss. 110(6) of the Act, upon which the Appellants rely, the RAD may hold a hearing if, in its opinion, there is documentary evidence referred to in ss. 110(3) of the Act of the that raises a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the Appellants, that is central to the RPD's decision, and that, if accepted, would justify allowing or rejecting the refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence under ss. 110(3) must be understood in relation to ss. 110(4).
propositions.quote: In this appeal, the documentary evidence referred to in ss. 110(3) of the Act must be understood in relation to ss. 110(4) of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: The court states ss. 110(6) allows hearing if new evidence raises serious credibility issue central to RPD decision; evidence under ss. 110(3) must meet ss. 110(4) criteria.

propositions.text: Ss. 110(3), (4) and (6) together mean RAD must not hold hearing unless new evidence raises serious credibility issue central to RPD decision and could justify claim outcome.
propositions.quote: When read together, ss. 110(3), (4) and (6) of the Act establish that the RAD must not hold a hearing in an appeal such as this unless there is new evidence, in which case the RAD may hold a hearing if that new evidence raises a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the Appellants, is central to the RPD's decision, and that, if accepted, would justify allowing or rejecting the refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the combined ss. 110(3), (4), (6) require new evidence raising serious credibility issue to justify hearing.

propositions.text: No new evidence accepted; must proceed without hearing; appellants' request for oral hearing denied.
propositions.quote: As no new evidence has been accepted as admissible by the RAD, I must proceed without a hearing. The Appellants' request for an oral hearing is denied.

paragraphs.summary: The court denies the appellants' request for an oral hearing as no new evidence was accepted.

propositions.text: RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness standard but may defer in limited circumstances where RPD has advantage.
propositions.quote: The RAD reviews RPD decisions on a standard of correctness. In limited circumstances, the RPD may have a meaningful advantage over the RAD in assessing evidence that was before the RPD. In those cases, the RAD will show deference to the RPD.

propositions.text: In this appeal, correctness standard applied unless otherwise stated.
propositions.quote: In this appeal, I have applied the correctness standard unless specifically stated otherwise.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness standard, deferring only in limited cases; here correctness standard applied.

propositions.text: Based on independent analysis including RPD hearing transcript, court finds no RPD error.
propositions.quote: Based on my independent analysis of the evidence, including my reading of the transcript of the hearing before the RPD, I do not find that the RPD erred.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error in the RPD decision after independent analysis including hearing transcript.

propositions.text: RPD found Black Eagles lack central leadership, command, defined structure, and are unstable with little evidence of systemic operation.
propositions.quote: In its decision, the RPD found that based on credible and undisputed documentary evidence, more particularly in the National Documentation Package (NDP), the Black Eagles do not have a central leadership, a central command nor a defined structure like other paramilitary organizations. They are unstable and there is little evidence to suggest that they operate like a systemic organization.

propositions.text: RPD concluded Black Eagles are not nearly the force claimed by appellant.
propositions.quote: In summary, the RPD concluded that the Black Eagles "is not nearly the force that you [XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX] claim it to be".

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found Black Eagles lack central leadership and structure and are not as powerful as appellant claims.

propositions.text: Appellants allege Black Eagles are agent of harm and risks need not come only from groups with central leadership.
propositions.quote: In their Memorandum, the Appellants allege that their agent of harm is the Black Eagles and that risks need not emanate only from groups that have a "central leadership".

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue Black Eagles are their agent of harm and risk can come from groups without central leadership.

propositions.text: For serious possibility of persecution, agent of harm must have means and motivation.
propositions.quote: The courts have established that for there to be a serious possibility of persecution, the agent of harm must have the means and the motivation.

propositions.text: RPD correctly found Black Eagles lack dominant presence, command, structure and territorial control to target individuals.
propositions.quote: While I understand the Appellants' argument, in the case at hand, I believe that the RPD is correct in its determination that the Black Eagles' lack of dominant presence, command and structure and territorial control make it unable to target and reach a particular individual.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites law requiring means and motivation for persecution and finds RPD correct that Black Eagles lack capacity to target individuals.

propositions.text: Due to credibility issues, insufficient evidence on balance of probabilities that Black Eagles can target or desire to harm appellants.
propositions.quote: Because of the credibility issues that I will deal with below, I find that there is insufficient evidence, on a balance of probabilities, to prove that the Black Eagles have the capacity or desire to target and harm the Appellants.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows 'Black Eagles' name can be used by anyone engaging in criminal activity including street gangs.
propositions.quote: In fact, the documentary evidence on file, including that provided by the Appellants before the RPD, indicates that the name "Black Eagles" can be used by anyone engaging in criminal activity, including street gangs.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds insufficient evidence that Black Eagles can or want to harm appellants; name can be used by various criminals.

propositions.text: Appellant alleged receiving threatening pamphlet in 2017 but did not report it to police or family and continued activities.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX alleged having received a threatening pamphlet in XXXX 2017. He testified that he did not bring it to the attention of the police because he did not consider it serious enough to report. He also did not mention it to XXXX nor his family because he did not want them to feel threatened by its contents. He then testified that he continued his activities despite the alleged threat.

propositions.text: RPD found explanations for not reporting pamphlet unreasonable.
propositions.quote: The RPD found these explanations to be unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's explanations for not reporting a threatening pamphlet unreasonable.

propositions.text: Appellants submit appellant felt compelled to continue activism due to its nature and importance.
propositions.quote: In their Memorandum, the Appellants submit that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX felt compelled to continue his political and social activism because of the nature of that activism and how he felt it was important.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the appellant felt compelled to continue activism because of its nature and importance.

propositions.text: XXXX testified he continued work for enjoyment, not compulsion
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX testified that he continued the work because he enjoyed the work, not because he felt compelled to continue.

propositions.text: No obligation to cease activism to prove fears are legitimate
propositions.quote: The Appellants submit in their Memorandum that there is no obligation on a refugee claimant to cease political or social activism to demonstrate that his fears are legitimate.

propositions.text: Continuing work for enjoyment after threats undermines credibility about threat seriousness
propositions.quote: I do find that continuing work for the sake of enjoyment, after having received threats to his and his family's lives for the sake of his personal enjoyment, undermines XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX's credibility about the seriousness of the threats he alleges having received.

paragraphs.summary: Witness testified he continued work for enjoyment; appellants argue no obligation to cease activism; court finds continuing work after threats undermines credibility.

propositions.text: Not reporting threatening pamphlet contradicts claim of life threat and undermines claim of no police protection
propositions.quote: Not reporting the threatening pamphlet because, according to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, he did not take it seriously, contradicts his allegations in his BOC that he felt his life was threatened.

propositions.text: Not sharing threat info with family or XXXX undermines claim of serious threat
propositions.quote: It is also unreasonable for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, who views the threat seriously to include it as part of the basis of his refugee claim, but does not share any of the information with his family so it may protect itself nor with XXXX so that it may take the appropriate measures to protect its member.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds not reporting pamphlet contradicts life threat claim and not sharing info with family or XXXX undermines claim of serious threat.

propositions.text: Police protection against Black Eagles is not available
propositions.quote: In their Memorandum, the Appellants argue that police protection against the Black Eagles is not available but have not provided any persuasive evidence to that effect.

propositions.text: Father's complaint to police was rejected for lack of evidence and he lacked details
propositions.quote: when XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX's father testified about the highway attack that he was a victim of, he added that his complaint to police was rejected for lack of evidence and that he was unable to provide details about the incident.

propositions.text: XXXX did not report threatening pamphlet to police
propositions.quote: In the case of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, he chose in one instance not to report the threatening pamphlet to police.

propositions.text: XXXX did not disclose all info to police about threats during attack in mother's car
propositions.quote: In another instance, when he was attacked in his mother's car, he did not disclose all of the information to police, more particularly that he had received threats related to his social and political activities.

propositions.text: Evidence does not support appellants' argument that police protection is unavailable against Black Eagles
propositions.quote: In my view, the evidence, both testimonial and documentary, does not support the Appellants' argument that there is no police protection in Colombia against the Black Eagles.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue no police protection; evidence shows father's complaint rejected for lack of evidence; XXXX did not fully report threats; court finds no support for no police protection claim.

propositions.text: RPD found failure to reveal pamphlet contents to police, XXXX and family undermines credibility
propositions.quote: The RPD's finding that the failure of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to have revealed the contents of the threatening pamphlet to the police, XXXX and his family undermines his credibility as to the seriousness of the threat is correct.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found failure to reveal pamphlet contents to police, XXXX and family undermines credibility; court agrees.

propositions.text: XXXX testified police told him to stop political activities and activism
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX testified that he was stopped by the police who told him to stop his political activities and social activism.

propositions.text: RPD asked why police complaint did not mention this important info
propositions.quote: Asked by the RPD why this important information was not mentioned in his complaint to the police, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX replied that was what the general prosecutor wrote down.

propositions.text: RPD asked why info was not in BOC
propositions.quote: Asked by the RPD as to why this information was not in his BOC, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. replied that at the time of filling out his BOC, he "did not realize everything".

paragraphs.summary: XXXX testified police told him to stop activism; RPD asked why complaint and BOC omitted this info; XXXX said prosecutor wrote complaint and he did not realize everything for BOC.

propositions.text: Explanations for missing info in complaint are unsatisfactory and undermine credibility
propositions.quote: These explanations are not satisfactory. To begin with, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX has a XXXX education. He was able to read and understand the contents of the complaint. His signature also appears on the document. It is unlikely that the general prosecutor would not write down such important information in the complaint. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX did not demonstrate that he had taken the necessary steps to have all the information put down in writing in his complaint by the prosecutor general. These unreasonable explanations regarding the missing information in his complaint undermine his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds explanations for missing info in complaint unsatisfactory and undermining credibility.

propositions.text: Omissions in BOC may legitimately be considered as lack of credibility
propositions.quote: Where a refugee claimant fails to mention important facts in his or her BOC, this may legitimately be considered by the Board to be an omission that goes to lack of credibility.

propositions.text: Omission of info about political risk in BOC is central and undermines credibility
propositions.quote: I find that the information omitted from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX's BOC is central to his refugee claim, namely that he is at risk because of his political activities and social activism. This omission is important and undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Court states omissions in BOC may show lack of credibility; finds omission of political risk info central and undermining credibility.

propositions.text: Father alleged two attacks by Black Eagles, one on highway eight hours from home
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX's father alleged that he was involved in two incidents involving the Black Eagles. The first one happened when he was being stopped on the highway eight hours away from home and threatened by the Black Eagles because of his son's political and social activities.

propositions.text: No persuasive evidence Black Eagles could attack so far without command or regional control
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX has not provided any persuasive evidence of how such an attack could take place eight hours away from his father's home by an organization without any command structure nor regional control.

paragraphs.summary: Father alleged two Black Eagles attacks; court finds no persuasive evidence Black Eagles could attack so far without command or control.

propositions.text: Second attack on father occurred when son had already left country
propositions.quote: The second incident occurred when his father was attacked on his motorcycle and threatened because of his son's activities. However, at the time of the alleged incident, his son, already left the country.

paragraphs.summary: Second attack on father occurred when son had already left country.

propositions.text: RPD correctly concluded father's attacks were random criminal violence due to lack of evidence of Black Eagles' ability
propositions.quote: Given the lack of persuasive evidence about the ability of the Black Eagles to carry out the alleged attacks, the RPD's conclusion that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX's father was in fact a victim of random criminal violence in both incidents is correct.

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees RPD correctly concluded father's attacks were random criminal violence due to lack of evidence of Black Eagles' ability.

propositions.text: XXXX travelled to USA in 2018 and returned to Colombia hoping situation settled
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX travelled to the USA in XXXX 2018 and stayed there until XXXX 2018, when he decided to return to Colombia. Asked by the RPD why he returned to the country where his alleged agents of persecution operated, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX replied that he had hoped that things had settled down.

propositions.text: RPD found explanation for return unreasonable and undermining credibility
propositions.quote: The RPD found this explanation, in light of the death threats that he had allegedly received, unreasonable and that it undermined his credibility.

propositions.text: Court agrees returning to country with death threats undermines credibility
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD. By returning to a country in which he received death threats, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX was in fact getting closer to his agents of persecution who threatened his life and that of his family. His actions and unsatisfactory explanations for returning to Colombia undermine his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: XXXX travelled to USA then returned to Colombia hoping situation settled; RPD and court find explanation unreasonable and undermining credibility.

propositions.text: XXXX did not claim asylum in USA during 4 months because he did not think of it
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX also testified not having claimed asylum in the USA while he was there for a period of 4 months because he did not think of it.

propositions.text: Failure to claim asylum at first opportunity is relevant to credibility assessment
propositions.quote: While failure to claim refugee status may not be in itself decisive, it is a relevant element that the RPD can take into account when assessing the credibility of an applicant as it is reasonable to expect that an applicant would make a claim at the first possible opportunity.

propositions.text: Courts hold failure to claim asylum indicates lack of subjective fear and undermines credibility
propositions.quote: The failure to do so has consistently been held by the Courts to indicate a lack of subjective fear and thus undermine an applicant's credibility because it can be construed as inconsistent with the behaviours of someone who genuinely fears for his life.

propositions.text: RPD reasonably drew adverse inference on credibility due to failure to claim asylum without satisfactory explanation
propositions.quote: In the case at hand, given the lack of a satisfactory explanation for not claiming asylum, the RPD reasonably drew an adverse inference as to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: XXXX did not claim asylum in USA; failure to claim asylum relevant to credibility; courts hold it undermines credibility; RPD reasonably drew adverse inference.

propositions.text: Failure to provide documentation is relevant to credibility
propositions.quote: Failure to provide documentation

paragraphs.summary: Failure to provide documentation is relevant to credibility.

propositions.text: RPD asked to see original documents; XXXX said he left them in Colombia to avoid traveling with them
propositions.quote: The RPD asked XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to see the original documents in support of his allegations. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX replied that he had left them in Colombia because he did not want to travel with them.

propositions.text: RPD found explanation unreasonable and that it undermined credibility
propositions.quote: The RPD found this explanation unreasonable and decided that it undermined his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: RPD asked for original documents; XXXX said he left them in Colombia; RPD found explanation unreasonable and undermining credibility.

propositions.text: Article 11 of RPD Rules requires claimants to provide acceptable documents or explain absence
propositions.quote: Article 11 of the Refugee Protection Division Rules states that claimants must provide acceptable documents establishing the elements of their claim. In absence of the documents, the claimant must explain why he has not provided the documents and what steps were taken to obtain them.

propositions.text: XXXX did not provide documentary evidence of political party membership or work for candidate XXXX
propositions.quote: For instance, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX did not provide any documentary evidence of his membership in a political party or the work he was allegedly carrying out for the candidate, XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: RPD Rules require documents or explanation; XXXX did not provide evidence of political party membership or work for candidate.

propositions.text: XXXX arrived in Canada in 2019; hearing was December 23, 2019
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX arrived in Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2019 while the hearing took place on December 23, 2019.

propositions.text: XXXX had ample time to have documents sent to Canada but made no effort or explanation; RPD's decision that this undermined credibility is correct
propositions.quote: This XXXX XXXX XXXX period between his arrival and the hearing provided him ample time to have the documents sent to Canada. Absent any effort to retrieve the documents during this period or any explanation as to why no efforts were made, I find that the RPD's decision that this undermined his credibility to be correct.

paragraphs.summary: XXXX arrived in Canada months before hearing; had time to get documents but made no effort; court agrees this undermines credibility.

propositions.text: RAD agrees with RPD that appellants have not established Black Eagles' ability or desire to harm them
propositions.quote: the RAD agrees with the RPD's finding that the Appellants have not established, on a balance of probabilities, that their agent of persecution, the Black Eagles, has the desire or the ability to put their lives or safety in peril should they return to Colombia.

propositions.text: Appellants have not established they were threatened due to social activism and political activities
propositions.quote: The RAD further finds that the Appellants have not established, on a balance of probabilities, that they were threatened with harm by individuals in Colombia because of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX's social activism and political activities.

paragraphs.summary: RAD agrees with RPD that appellants failed to prove Black Eagles' ability or desire to harm or threats due to social activism.

propositions.text: No serious possibility of persecution if appellants return to Colombia
propositions.quote: Therefore, the RAD finds that there is not a serious possibility of persecution should the Appellants return to Colombia.

propositions.text: Appellants failed to establish well-founded fear of persecution under s. 96 and are not persons in need of protection under s. 97
propositions.quote: The RAD therefore concludes that the Appellants have failed to establish a well-founded fear of persecution under section 96 of the Act, and, for the same reasons, the RAD finds that the Appellants are not persons in need of protection or at a risk to life, or at risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, or in danger of torture as set out in section 97 of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: RAD finds no serious possibility of persecution and appellants failed to establish fear under s.96 or protection need under s.97.

propositions.text: RAD confirms RPD decision that appellants are neither Convention refugees under s. 96 nor persons in need of protection under s. 97
propositions.quote: Pursuant to Section 111(1)(a) of the Act, the RAD confirms the decision of the RPD that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX are neither Convention refugees under section 96 nor persons in need of protection under section 97 of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: RAD confirms RPD decision appellants are neither Convention refugees under s.96 nor persons in need of protection under s.97.

propositions.text: Appeals are dismissed
propositions.quote: The appeals are dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: Appeals are dismissed.
